name: Finland
summary_text: Finland is very safe. A 2023 reform removed the sterilisation requirement for legal gender recognition (Finland was the last EU country to do so), but a medical statement is still required — not full self-determination. Finland issued a US travel advisory for trans citizens in March 2025. The Police University College reports record hate-crime levels (1,808 suspected cases in 2024, up 13% since 2023 — the majority racist, but sexual orientation is among the identified motives). There are no documented severe trans-specific incidents (no tourist-rape, mob violence, or police-brutality case). Bathrooms are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation, and the Schengen border poses no trans-specific friction.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on Finland: record 1,808 suspected hate crimes in 2025 (+13% since 2023), with sexual orientation and gender identity recurrent motives (12% of cases); Finland's first conversion-practices case prosecuted as assault (convictions in March); Parliament endorsed a citizens' initiative to ban conversion practices (125-49) in March, though a full ban remained pending.

sources.title: New record in suspected hate crimes - Police University College
sources.claim_summary: Finland's Police University College (Nov 2025): 1,808 suspected hate crimes reported to police in 2024 - the highest figure ever; defamation and assault most common; motive is decisive as the law does not recognise 'hate crime' as a distinct offence.

sources.title: Denmark and Finland urge caution for US-bound transgender people | Denmark | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (March 2025): Denmark and Finland updated travel advice urging caution for transgender people travelling to the US amid US gender-document policy changes - Denmark advised trans travellers to contact the US embassy before travel. Notable example of trans-specific official travel advisories.

sources.title: An 'open wound': Europe's trans community reckons with decades of sterilisation requirements | Investigate Europe
sources.claim_summary: Investigate Europe (Sept 2025) 'The Cruel Condition': investigation into Europe's sterilisation requirements for legal gender recognition - thousands of trans people pushed into invasive surgery (case study of a Czech-required orchiectomy); Finland is among countries whose historical/current frameworks are examined.

sources.title: Parliament approves law to allow children of same-sex couples to have two mothers from birth | Yle
sources.claim_summary: Yle News (Feb 2018): Finland's Parliament approved recognising both women in same-sex partnerships as mothers from birth (122-42) - amending the Maternity Act to remove the adoption requirement for the non-birth mother.

sources.title: Same-sex marriage law goes into effect in Finland | Yle
sources.claim_summary: Yle News (March 2017): Finland's same-sex marriage law went into effect - same-sex couples also gained the right to adopt; ~41 couples scheduled to marry in the first week.

sources.title: Gay marriage initiative proceeds to Parliament with 162,000 backers | Yle
sources.claim_summary: Yle News (Sept 2013): the 'Tahdon2013' ('I Do') citizens' initiative for same-sex marriage proceeded to Parliament with 162,000 signatures - the largest citizens' initiative to date in Finland.
